components.css: .ds-btn-signal { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; background: #2138b8; color: #f4f6ff; border: 1px solid rgba(157,176,255,0.28); border-radius: 0; padding: 0.75rem 1.25rem; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.76rem; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.12em; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s, box-shadow 0.2s, transform 0.2s, border-color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-signal:hover { background: #2c47d4; border-color: rgba(157,176,255,0.5); transform: translateY(-1px); box-shadow: 0 10px 28px -12px rgba(61,99,255,0.6); } .ds-btn-signal:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #9db0ff; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview: A portfolio drawn, not decorated — cobalt draughting ink laid over a warm engineering sheet. The canvas is a near-black ink carrying a two-layer measurement grid and a fine film grain, lit from the top-left like a drafting lamp. Type is a high-contrast serif for statements and a monospace for every coordinate; diagrams are framed, captioned Plates, not screenshots in cards. The one live color is cobalt — it marks signal, never fills space. The system's discipline is the argument: exact spacing, measured contrast, and a single restrained accent read as the same engineering rigor the work claims.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-ink canvas with an ever-present engineering grid + grain (never a flat solid).
Cobalt as signal only: accent strokes, active nav, primary CTA, one italic word.
Sharp corners everywhere; registration ticks instead of rounded cards.
Monospace coordinate labels carry all metadata.
Serif display statements over monospace scaffolding — contrast, not costume.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Cobalt is signal, not decoration. As primary accent it appears on ≤10% of any screen — strokes, active state, primary CTA, one emphasis word. The categorical domain hues are the one sanctioned exception, and only when color carries domain meaning.

rules.name: The Three-Domain Rule
rules.body: Jade / cobalt / violet mean Product·AI / Cloud / Security — and nothing else. Exactly three hues, each a fixed meaning, always paired with a text label (color never the sole signal). No fourth categorical hue; never repurpose one for decoration.

rules.name: The Warm-Ink Rule
rules.body: The neutral ramp is warm (bone → ink); the accent is cool (cobalt). Never warm the accent or cool the neutrals to match; the temperature split is the identity.

rules.name: The Coordinate Label Rule
rules.body: All metadata is monospace, uppercase, wide-tracked, prefixed with a marker (§00, Plate 01, a two-digit index). Metadata never uses the serif or body sans.

rules.name: The One Italic Rule
rules.body: Emphasis in a display statement is a single Fraunces italic word, optionally in cobalt. Never bold the serif; never italicize a whole line.

rules.name: The Flat-Sheet Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and separated by 1px lines, never by shadow. The single exception is the cobalt Signal Bloom on primary-button hover.

dos: Do keep the engineering grid + grain present on every page background; never ship a flat solid ink fill.
Do hold cobalt to ≤10% of any screen — strokes, active state, primary CTA, one italic word.
Do set all metadata in monospace uppercase with a marker prefix.
Do keep body text at Bone Dim (#c7c0b4) or brighter; verify ≥4.5:1 on ink before shipping any new muted text.
Do frame diagrams as captioned Plates recolored into the duotone, with registration ticks.
Do provide a prefers-reduced-motion fallback for every reveal and transition.
donts: Don't reintroduce the generic dark-neon dev site: slate-950 + cyan glow, glassmorphism panels, or radial gradient mesh.
Don't add flashy, animation-heavy spectacle. Motion is one page-load reveal plus honest hover feedback.
Don't round corners (except the 3px on inline code). No rounded cards, no pill radii.
Don't use neutral gray drop shadows; separate surfaces with 1px lines.
Don't warm the cobalt accent or cool the bone/ink neutrals to match.
Don't set metadata, eyebrows, or labels in the serif or body sans.
